own verb

possess

also possess, belong to, whose is it?, it’s mine, belong, it belongs to

classical

Ov. Met. 8.187: nōn possidet āëra
Cic. Quinct. 25 (Lewis & Short)

possideō, possidēre, possēdī, possessum

verb, second conjugation, transitive

own, possess

“Whose is it?” is Cujus est?; “it’s mine”, meum est (Hor. Ep. 1.16.35). The owner is dominus. “Belong to” is usually the genitive of the owner with esse: Aegōnis est, “it belongs to Aegon”; the question is cujum?, “whose?” (Verg. Ecl. 3.1). For belonging to a group, see member.

Examples

  • pōne, meum est

    put it down, it’s mineHor. Ep. 1.16.35

  • omnia possideat, nōn possidet āëra Mīnōs

    Minos may own everything, but he doesn’t own the airOv. Met. 8.187

  • Dīc mihi, Dāmoetā, cujum pecus, an Meliboeī? — Nōn, vērum Aegōnis; nūper mihi trādidit Aegōn.

    Tell me, Damoetas, whose flock is that? Meliboeus’s? — No, it’s Aegon’s; Aegon handed it over to me the other day.Verg. Ecl. 3.1–2

See also own, member.
